4377
# The RFC 0029 journal is new, so no test on main covers it. Redundant tests were merged and each kept test turned red under at least one mutant of the code it covers.
# Engine journal unit tests: the §5.1 row states (a change over a sent or held row, a value returning to the one in flight), each §5.2 result holding, superseding or ending rows, the bounded history, delete seen lists, replays after a loss, the journal generator's own stream, and the legacy id vectors.
# Engine intents: the row each scan, create, edit, move and delete writes; commits naming intents only when the server announces them; every result kind (APPLIED, APPLIED_RENAMED, SUPERSEDED, CONFLICT_COPY, MERGED_INTO, ID_EXISTS); compact held rows written out unchanged on every trigger and through the store; the backfill of a store from an earlier release; the first listing that names intents.
# Engine commit: an op the server supersedes ends for each op kind unless the journal sends it again, a later local edit survives it, and an edit after a conflict copy names the copy's version.
# Sim conformance: the harness checks intents, lineage and storage restores, so the RFC 0029 scenarios that main's reference space skips run.
# Sim space rules: the reference space's intent rules: legacy ids for the root, malformed intents refused, garbage collection and purged nodes, a storage restore minting intents, and the field_intents announcement.
# Sim devices and recovery: rewinds, rollbacks, lost edits and lost renames across restores with intents on, the GUN-1012 known red with its exact message, and resends that go out without an intent.
# Store: the journal tables, the intents of R and S and the backfill marker survive a reopen and an upgrade.
# Review follow-ups: two loads of one stored state mint distinct intents, a nested delete lists each intent once, the engine memory test runs with the intents the server returns, and the §5.1 30-day end of a purged node's journal state, its reset, the rows it keeps, and the seen list a backfilled delete of a folder L no longer holds takes from S.
# Integration with main's DeleteUndone oracle: the folder merge and S2 in a move's deletes, the P1 recovery order, the oracle's view of RFC 0029 line 147 and its seen lists, a re-trashed child deleted under the trash's intent with what the trash holds as seen, and loads of one stored state, a journal restore and a store rollback that never mint an ID twice.
# DeleteUndone's elsewhere half: a reference-space server that keeps a conflict copy of each trashed file is caught, and the five named lost-edit tests where the resent write outlives the delete carry their exact GUN-665 reds.
# Battery fixes: a_create_superseded_on_a_purged_node_gives_way_to_the_purge_and_is_not_created_again keeps RFC 0029 §5.2 for a create the server supersedes because it purged the node: S takes L's place and nothing is created again under the purged id. The existing superseded tests cover only trashed nodes, which R still holds. a_restart_mints_intents_it_never_minted_before keeps the sim's crash restart from minting intent ids the device already sent. loads_of_one_stored_state_never_mint_the_same_id covers the driver's load, not the sim's restart.
# Store engine_state drop: engine_state_dropped applies the drop alone to a store whose engine_state holds its id_generator row and checks that the table goes while every other table keeps its rows. The harness checks only the preserved tables of the whole upgrade, so it can't show that the drop touches nothing else. It also applies the drop again to a store with no engine_state, as an internal store that ran an earlier head's migrations holds.
# Read-path loads: a_store_that_owes_its_journal_adopts_its_renumbered_disk_and_loads loads a store with no journal_state row through the root check's renumbered-disk adoption and through Folder::load, both of which read in a query_only transaction. No other test empties journal_state before a folder loads.
# Compact NodeId makes several journal test assertions wrap across more lines. The recovery Delete tests also check the wire view of a restored version and that a later edit still prevents the Delete with intents on.
# #912 trash groups: a_backfill_keeps_the_trash_group_of_a_trashed_past_position and the journal_backfill_trash_group upgrade case check that the backfill keeps a trashed past position's group as its trashed status intent, in the engine and through the release fixture's migrations; no other test backfills a past position with a trash group.
# The kept-folder purge race verifies no journal or wire use of old IDs when the only edit is to a rules file, and fresh IDs and exact paths when a new file appears.
# #911 move bases: journal_after_move_bases stages the alpha6 fixture through every named migration but the journal and checks the folded place intent, the Held base and place history from a verified move history, the Sent base and history from move_bases, and #911's lost-rename outcome, each against rev, place, trash and null controls. Two intents tests check the same seeding in the engine alone, and a_legacy_place_intent_never_replaces_the_place_a_row_holds checks that the legacy column only fills a missing place and that writing the node with a new place clears the column. No #911 test reads the journal.
# KOI-1230 kept-folder guards: a_synced_file_added_to_a_kept_folder_uploads_it_as_a_new_folder also checks that no journal row places into the old folder ID, and a_folder_this_device_made_keeps_no_journal_rows_once_it_is_kept checks that a kept folder ends its rows. Each fails without its guard line.
# Purge of a held-apart folder: a_folder_held_apart_from_a_rename_the_rules_leave_out_is_sent_under_a_new_id_once_the_server_purges_it checks that a folder this device holds at its own name, because the rules leave out the server's name for it, is sent again under a fresh id with its held entry when the server deletes and purges it before the device acts on the delete. RFC 0029 supersedes a create that names a purged node, and the only other test of this path is #818's device test.
